cargo-val
Run Rust tests as isolated processes with streaming discovery.

Usage: cargo val [OPTIONS] [FILTER] [-- <TEST-ARGS>...]

Options:
  -h, --help       Print help
  -V, --version    Print version
      --exact      Match FILTER against the full test name
      --fail-fast  Stop launching tests after the first failure (default)
      --no-fail-fast
                   Run every selected test; also forwarded to Cargo
      --max-fail <N>
                   Stop launching tests after N failures (N >= 1); --fail-fast is N = 1
      --no-tests <fail|warn|pass>
                   What a run that selects zero tests does (default: fail)
      --process <auto|shard|test>
                   Tests per OS process: shard groups them, test runs one each (default: auto)
      --output <auto|rich|plain>
                   Rich display for terminals, append-only lines for logs (default: auto)
  -E, --filterset <EXPR>
                   Select tests with a nextest filterset subset (see below)
      --target-dir <isolated|shared|PATH>
                   Where the build directories live (see below; default: shared)
      --test-timeout <secs|none>
                   The deadline every test is declared to have, shown as limit= on RUNNING lines (default: none)
      --heartbeat <secs>
                   Seconds between RUNNING lines for the oldest test in flight (default: the build-time heartbeat_secs, 10)
      --exit-with-parent
                   Kill the running tests and exit when the parent process exits (macOS, Linux; default: off)

Cargo options such as -p, --package, --test, --lib, -F, --features, -m,
--manifest-path, --target, --profile, and -j/--jobs are forwarded to Cargo.
-j/--jobs keeps Cargo's meaning (build jobs).

Test arguments after `--`:
  --ignored                  Run only ignored tests
  --include-ignored          Run ignored and regular tests (not with --ignored)
  --test-threads <N>         Live test processes at once; also --test-threads=<N>

Test concurrency, highest precedence first (valid range 1..=64):
  1. --test-threads <N> after `--`
  2. RUST_TEST_THREADS
  3. CARGO_VAL_JOBS
  4. the build-time default (CARGO_VAL_BUILD_JOBS; shard mode: CARGO_VAL_BUILD_SHARD_JOBS, default 2x the cores)

Stop policy, highest precedence first (default: fail fast, --max-fail 1):
  1. --fail-fast, --no-fail-fast, or --max-fail <N> (the last one given wins)
  2. CARGO_VAL_MAX_FAIL=<N>
  3. CARGO_VAL_FAIL_FAST=<true|false>
On a trip, no further tests launch, children already running finish normally,
and the report counts listed tests that were not run.

No-tests policy, highest precedence first (default: fail):
  1. --no-tests <fail|warn|pass>
  2. CARGO_VAL_NO_TESTS
fail and warn print "no tests to run" with the selection to stderr; fail exits 4,
warn and pass exit 0.

Process mode, highest precedence first (default: auto):
  1. --process <auto|shard|test>
  2. CARGO_VAL_PROCESS
  3. the build-time default (CARGO_VAL_BUILD_PROCESS)
auto shards on a Windows target and runs one test per process elsewhere. A shard child
runs a contiguous group of a binary's tests (about one child per job; fewer names when
the command line limit is reached) and every test is still reported on its own line; a
test that takes its process down is reported FAIL and the tests behind it run again.

Output mode, highest precedence first (default: auto):
  1. --output <auto|rich|plain>
  2. CARGO_VAL_OUTPUT
  3. the build-time default (CARGO_VAL_BUILD_OUTPUT)
auto is rich only when standard output is an interactive terminal (a console on Windows)
and CI is unset or empty and TERM is not dumb; a pipe, a file, CI, or a dumb terminal gets
plain. plain never emits ANSI escapes. NO_COLOR suppresses color in every mode.
Plain output is append-only, one line per event, labels padded to nine columns:
  START/PASS/FAIL/IGNORED  <binary id>  <test>  [<secs>s]  [(solo rerun)]
  a failure's captured streams follow its FAIL line between "------ stdout: <id> <test> ------"
  and "------ end stdout ------" (stderr likewise), then at the end: the total: line,
  SUMMARY passed=P failed=F ignored=I not_run=N wall=S, one FAILED line per failure, and
  RERUN, a cargo val command that reruns only the failures. GITHUB_ACTIONS=true also wraps
  each block in ::group::/::endgroup:: and prints one ::error annotation per failure.

Test timeout, highest precedence first (default: none):
  1. --test-timeout <secs|none>
  2. CARGO_VAL_TEST_TIMEOUT=<secs|none>
secs is a whole number from 1 to 4294967. It declares a deadline for the RUNNING line; it does not kill a test.

Heartbeat, highest precedence first (default: the heartbeat_secs sizing constant, 10):
  1. --heartbeat <secs>
  2. CARGO_VAL_HEARTBEAT_SECS=<secs>
  3. the build-time default (the heartbeat_secs sizing constant)
In plain output, every interval while a test is in flight prints one line for the oldest:
  RUNNING  <binary id>  <test>  <age>s  [limit=<secs>s]  (oldest of N running)


Exit with parent, highest precedence first (default: off):
  1. --exit-with-parent
  2. CARGO_VAL_EXIT_WITH_PARENT=<on|off|1|0>
  3. the build-time default (CARGO_VAL_BUILD_EXIT_WITH_PARENT=<on|off>)
Off, a run keeps going when its parent exits, as a nohup or backgrounded run must. On, the first
parent exit kills every running test and ends the run with status 129; a test harness that may be
SIGKILLed sets it so no run outlives it.

Ignored tests: `#[ignore]`d tests are listed per test binary with `--list --ignored`, are
not launched by default, and are reported IGNORED and counted separately. CARGO_VAL_IGNORED
=<skip|only|include> sets the mode; --ignored / --include-ignored win. Each launched test
is classified by its libtest `test result:` line: 0 passed is never PASS, and an exact
launch that ran no test body is an error naming the test.

Filterset (-E, --filterset, or CARGO_VAL_FILTERSET; the flag wins): predicates test(),
binary(), package(), all(), none(); operators and/&, or/|/+, not/!, - (difference) and
parentheses (not binds tighter than and/-, which bind tighter than or). Matchers: bare
text (contains for test(), glob for binary() and package(), as in nextest), ~contains,
=exact, #glob (* ? [..] [!..]). /regex/ and glob {a,b} are not supported and fail with a
caret before anything is built. Excluded tests are never launched and count as filtered.

Test executables and bins: a test or bench executable is not listed or launched until
every bin target of its package has been built, so env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_<name>") exists.
The bin set comes from one `cargo metadata`; without it the executable waits
for build-finished. A failed build launches none of the waiting executables.
CARGO_VAL_BIN_GATE=off disables the wait; CARGO_VAL_LOG=debug prints one stderr line
per gate decision.

Build directories (--target-dir, or CARGO_VAL_TARGET_DIR; the flag wins; default shared):
  isolated  <cargo's target dir>/cargo-val/<workspace key>/test for the test build and
            .../doc for the doc build, so no other cargo process, rust-analyzer, or
            cargo val shares their build lock, and the two builds never wait on each other
  shared    cargo's own target dir (--target-dir, CARGO_TARGET_DIR, build.target-dir,
            <workspace>/target); every cargo process on it shares one build lock
  PATH      <PATH>/test and <PATH>/doc
cargo's target dir comes from `cargo metadata`. A child that blocks on a lock prints one
line: cargo-val: waiting for <lock> held by another cargo process (<dir>). The package
cache lock lives in CARGO_HOME and cannot be isolated. Isolated compiles dependencies
once more per workspace than plain `cargo test`, and the doc build compiles the library
a second time.

Summary: after the results, one line per test binary, then a total line with wall time:
  <binary>: discovered N, passed P, failed F, ignored I, filtered X
  total: discovered N, passed P, failed F, ignored I, filtered X, wall S.mmms
The binary id is the package name for a library and package::target otherwise. A binary
whose counts do not add up is an error naming it. A run that executed no test (passed +
failed = 0) follows --no-tests.

Exit status: 0 all selected tests passed, 1 a test failed, 2 invalid arguments or
settings or a driver failure or an invocation cargo refused, 3 the cargo build failed, 4 no
tests to run under the fail policy.

Doc tests: the default selection also runs `cargo test --doc` as one child at nice 10,
concurrently with the other tests; its doctests are reported and counted like any test.
--doc runs only doc tests. Any target flag (--lib, --bins, --bin, --examples, --example,
--tests, --test, --benches, --bench, --all-targets) without --doc excludes them, as in
Cargo. A package with no library target skips them with a notice; a run of 0 doc tests
prints "doc tests: running 0 tests". On a stop-policy trip the doc child is interrupted
only if it has not printed "running N tests"; otherwise it finishes normally.
